summary:
Approve. The integer BigInt conversion fixes the precision loss without changing fractional rounding; no correctness defects found.

Validation: all 46 Duration tests passed. A plain-node probe passed 12 integer cases covering exact conversions, equality, hashing, and HashSet lookup, plus four fractional-rounding cases. The reported positive and negative epoch-sized toHrTime outputs were exact.

Reported two non-blocking suggestions: retain regression tests for large-value equality/hash behavior and signed toHrTime output. Added validation results to both threads. Temporary probe removed; working tree clean. Broad checks and lint were intentionally not run, as requested.

params.title: Add a large-value equality/hash regression case
params.body: Non-blocking: the new assertion covers the conversion, but the PR also fixes cross-representation equality and hashing. The existing equality/hash test uses only small values (plus a power of two for overflow), so it does not pin the precision-loss case. Consider extending that test with `Duration.millis(1_760_450_000_123)` versus `Duration.nanos(1_760_450_000_123_000_000n)`, asserting `Equal.equals`, equal hashes, and HashSet lookup.

params.title: Pin the reported high-resolution conversion for both signs
params.body: Non-blocking: the motivating `toHrTime` example is not asserted in the committed tests. Consider adding `[1_760_450_000, 123_000_000]` for the positive epoch-sized input and `[-1_760_450_000, -123_000_000]` for its negative counterpart. This would cover the public symptom and ensure the exact integer path remains symmetric for signed durations, rather than only checking the positive bigint conversion.

toolCalls.result: reportFinding rejected: finding f1 is already anchored on packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts:569 ("Add a large-value equality/hash regression case"). Use updateThread({ id: "f1", body }) to add to it instead.

params.title: Pin the reported high-resolution conversion for both signs
params.body: Non-blocking: this shared conversion fixes the motivating `toHrTime` example too, but that public symptom is not asserted in the committed tests. Consider adding `[1_760_450_000, 123_000_000]` for the positive epoch-sized input and `[-1_760_450_000, -123_000_000]` for its negative counterpart in the `toHrTime` test. This would retain coverage for the reported output and the signed integer path rather than only checking positive bigint conversion.

Validation: `pnpm test --run packages/effect/test/Duration.test.ts` passed all 46 tests. A temporary scratchpad run with plain `node` checked exact conversion, Duration/Equal equality, hash agreement, and HashSet membership for 12 integer inputs, including both signs of the epoch-sized value, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, 2**53, and MAX_VALUE; all passed. This is a regression-coverage suggestion, not an observed runtime defect.

Probe result: the plain-node scratchpad returned `[1760450000, 123000000]` and `[-1760450000, -123000000]` for the positive/negative epoch-sized values. High-resolution conversion checks passed for all 12 integer inputs; four fractional rounding checks also passed. The scratchpad was removed afterward. The implementation currently behaves correctly; the suggestion is to retain these public-API checks as tests.
